system: You are a careful research assistant classifying public feedback. Output JSON only.
prompt:
Decide for each numbered item whether it is RELEVANT to a study of SIPs (systematic investment plans in mutual funds, incl. auto-invest / monthly mutual-fund investing) with three questions:
  (A) Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
  (B) What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing, reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it)?
  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

RELEVANT = the text describes the writer's own (or other investors') SIP experience, motives, expectations, behaviour or decisions that speak to A, B or C - including payment/mandate/app problems that make a SIP miss or stop.
NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

Return a JSON array with one object per item: [{"i": <item number>, "relevant": true|false}]

[7] (source: valuepickr; context: Beginner investing questions about Direct vs Regular mutual funds, mistakes and learning resources)
Hi @uno , I started investing in mutual funds when I was 24 years old. That was in 2002. In these 24 years, I have done SIP every month till last year. (I did pause SIP for 4 years in between, when I purchased a house and started EMIs). Sharing some learnings and I hope they help you…
 Just like you, I started with zero knowledge and too many questions. My journey can be broken into 3 phases
 Accumulation Stage (2002 ~ 2009) 
 Started with well known regular active equity funds (There were no index funds then. No direct option either). Most funds were well known funds like HDFC Prudence, Reliance Vision etc.
 My allocation was 100 % to equity.
 There was a massive crash in 2008. I did not stop SIPs for that. (I did stop in 2010 for my EMIs)
 Asset Allocation Stage (2012 ~ 2021) 
 The investment had grown substantial and the 2008 crash had taught me that drawdown can be massive. I started reading about asset allocation. Came up with a 60:40 debt strategy.
 Started diverting bulk of new SIPs to debt so as reach asset allocation of 60:40.
 Bucket Strategy Stage (2021 ~ now) 
 Investment has grown large enough to start focusing on corpus stability and withdrawals. I decided on a 4 bucket strategy.
 Asset allocation - 10 year expenditure is in debt. Remaining is all equity/Commodities etc.
 My suggestion to you from my journey above is this
 Start with a SIP in a Direct Index fund and keep it going. You dont have to work out the entire journey before taking the first step.
